card.name: Citation marks in social-science prose
card.fires_on: Scattered spots in general web essays on education, society and economics, such as an opening parenthesis before a citation or statistic, a comma after a book title, or a digit inside a year or code. No single word type fits all of them.

modes.label: Parenthesis before citation
modes.description: An opening bracket right after a statistic or claim, introducing a source or note.
modes.example: homeschooled?increased from 1.7 percent in 1999 to 2.2 percent in 2003<< (>>not shown in tables or figures). As

modes.label: Digit inside a year
modes.description: A digit partway through a historical year or reference number.
modes.example: International cooperation to end the traffic in women for the purpose of prostitution began in 18<<9>>9. In 1921

modes.label: Punctuation near an author or title
modes.description: A comma or the word author after a book title in a discussion of a work.
modes.example: In Human Capital<<,>> author Thomas O. Davenport explores this

card.writes: Suppresses technology-related words and slightly promotes shape and magnetic words, which is not a clear effect.
card.plain: It lights up at scattered citation-style spots in essays, like a bracket after a statistic or a digit inside a year.
